parsed.rationale: Although `PlaybackController` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` share four members (`installRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`, `removeRenderTap:()`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline itself found no meaningful overlap. More importantly, the two protocols model distinct domain responsibilities: `PlaybackController` is a high-level playback command surface (with `PlaybackState`, `PlaybackReason`-parameterised `play`/`stop`/`toggle`, and a loading indicator), while `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a lower-level, time-aware player interface (with `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `stateStream`, `timePositionStream`, and `eventStream`). Forcing a parent–child inheritance relationship would couple two protocols whose divergent signatures (`play:(reason:) throws` vs `play:()`, `PlaybackState` vs `PlayerState`) reflect intentionally different abstraction layers. The four overlapping method names are low-level audio-tap and stream utilities that are coincidentally shared, not evidence of a common abstraction.
